name: manual_566df2
claim: When 'git rebase --continue' repeats 'You must edit all merge conflicts and then mark them as resolved using git add' even though git status shows zero unmerged paths and 'git ls-files -u' is empty, the real blocker is downstream in a git hook (commit-msg/pre-commit) failing silently — run 'git commit --no-edit' directly to surface the hook's actual stderr instead of re-reading the stale rebase message.
conditions: rebase continue merge conflicts stale message hook stderr commit-msg CRLF bash carriage return

decisions.notes: 2026-07-03: the phrase persisted across multiple retries with a clean index. Direct 'git commit --no-edit' revealed the true error: 'env: bash\r: No such file or directory' — a CRLF-corrupted commit-msg hook script (scripts/git/check_commit_message.sh had Windows line endings from a cross-platform commit). Fixed by stripping \r and re-running scripts/git/install-local-hooks.sh.
